newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Safeway eyes margins, sales growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Safeway eyes margins, sales growth.

text.p: British supermarket group Safeway Plc wants to improve margins but is focused on remaining competitive, finance director Simon Laffin told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"We are obviously always trying to improve our gross margin but we have to remain fully competitive. We won't allow ourselves to get out of line with competition on pricing because it is still a very price-sensitive sector," he said.
Safeway said in a statement with full-year results that the gross margin was currently slightly down on the previous year, continuing the trend of the second half of last year.
Safeway said pre-tax profits were 430.1 million stg in the year ending March 29, up seven percent, and it paid out a total dividend of 14.10 pence per share compared with 12.75 pence.
It said current sales from existing stores were up 3.7 percent with prices down 0.9 percent, compared with 4.7 percent growth for the year, when inflation was running at two percent.
